thread:
evan: Hey runtime team — quick marketing ask for launch assets. We need a tiny, reproducible sanity pack that checks warmup vs coldstart behavior + quantized variants for the model family we'll be shouting about in the post. Can you run a few targeted reruns and drop a small artifact we can screenshot for the deck?

Evan: TL;DR asks:
- 1 x warmup sweep (simulate steady traffic for 10k requests, record p50/p95/p99 and warmup curve)
- 1 x coldstart heatmap (batch of fresh containers, 1 request each, 5k samples)
- Quantized variants: full-fp16, q4, q8 if available
- Long-context smoke: 8k token prompt tail case (100 samples)
- Stream on/off comparison (10 samples each)
- Please include simple JSON manifest with sample payloads and run commands 

kevin: Got it. Couple clarifying Qs: which exact model + quantization names? Also what workload distribution for the warmup (poisson, constant)?

evan: Use the model we've been using in the webinar slides: "redwood-x-7b" and the quant variants we tested last month (fp16, q4_0, q8_0). For warmup -> constant QPS ramp: 10rps -> 100rps over 5 minutes -> hold 100rps for 10 min. Coldstart: all requests hitting new replica group.

maria: Also need the sample prompts we used for the benchmark claim. Ideally 50 inputs that are representative (mix of short chat, long-form, code). We want to avoid cherry-picking. Can runtime share the exact sample IDs and raw inputs we can attach to the methodology note?

kevin: We can reuse the public sample cohort from /bench/samples/marketing_cohort_v2 — will pull 5k random rows for coldstart and 100 for long-context. We'll produce an artifact with MD5 of the payload file for provenance.

tom: For the deck, product wants p50/p95/p99 numbers and a tiny graph of latency vs request index for warmup. Can you produce a single PNG and the underlying CSV?

kevin: Yep. We'll output: latency_time_series.csv, quant_variant_summary.csv, coldstart_heatmap.png, warmup_curve.png, manifest.json (includes exact curl commands + token redaction).

anna: Are these results embargoed until launch? Marketing will draft language but need to know if any numbers are preliminary and could change after final runs.

evan: Embargo until launch week, yes. Flag anything 'experimental' in the manifest so we can call out caveats.

kevin: Understood. One more: do you want every run with KV cache warm vs cold? For the long-context tests cache behavior changes latency a lot.

evan: Good call — include both: cold KV cache (new session) and warm KV cache (follow-on request after same session).

runtime-bot: Scheduling jobs: bench-warmup-1765440001, bench-coldstart-1765440001, bench-quant-1765440001 queued on eng-runtime cluster pool-2. ETA 24-36h. Logs will be at https://internal.redwood/bench/runs/1765440001 once complete.

kevin: I'll also include a tiny runbook snippet for reproducibility. Example command we'll include in manifest (redacted token):

```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-x-7b","input":"<sample>","max_tokens":256,"stream":false}'
```

kevin: ETA for artifacts: ~36 hours. If marketing needs a quick screenshot earlier we can run a tiny smoke and drop warmup_curve_preview.png by EOD.

maria: That would be great — a preview PNG we can use for internal review is super helpful. Also: please tag me when the manifest is ready so I can check sample provenance.

kevin: Will do. Tagging plan: @maria in run notes + commit the manifest to internal bench bucket with MD5 + run metadata.

evan: Thanks all. If any of the quant variants fail (OOM or perf regressions) call it out explicitly in the manifest with the fallback used.

kevin: Copy. I'll post here when runs complete (or earlier if we have errors).
